evidence.claim: The IMF said the authorities had adopted prudent macroeconomic policies, most visibly by halting central bank financing to the government.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation and the Second Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement for the Democratic Republic of the Congo
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the authorities had adopted prudent macroeconomic policies, most visibly by halting central bank financing to the government.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF press release with explicit policy attribution and date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this describes the national authorities under Tshisekedi's government.
contrary_evidence: The same release says poverty remained very high and domestic arrears accumulated.

evidence.claim: The IMF said fragility continued to hinder inclusive growth, with 72.5 percent of the population in poverty and basic public services severely under-provisioned.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation and the Second Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement for the Democratic Republic of the Congo
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said fragility continued to hinder inclusive growth, with 72.5 percent of the population in poverty and basic public services severely under-provisioned.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF press release with direct macro and household welfare assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: these are national outcomes under the incumbent government, but not all are uniquely ruler-caused.
contrary_evidence: The same release reports growth at 6.2 percent in 2021 and stronger reserves.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the program remained satisfactory but that one structural benchmark was pending because a mining contract had not yet been published and two end-June 2022 benchmarks were slightly delayed.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation and the Second Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement for the Democratic Republic of the Congo
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the program remained satisfactory but that one structural benchmark was pending because a mining contract had not yet been published and two end-June 2022 benchmarks were slightly delayed.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF program-monitoring report with clear implementation detail.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this is about government implementation under Tshisekedi's administration.
contrary_evidence: The same report says four of five structural benchmarks were met.

evidence.claim: The IMF urged continued efforts to improve mining sector transparency, the anti-corruption and AML/CFT frameworks, the business climate, and governance to support diversification and competitiveness.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation and the Second Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement for the Democratic Republic of the Congo
evidence.excerpt: The IMF urged continued efforts to improve mining sector transparency, the anti-corruption and AML/CFT frameworks, the business climate, and governance to support diversification and competitiveness.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF guidance tied to the country's reform program.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the policy recommendations are directed at the incumbent authorities.
contrary_evidence: The same release says external shocks and inflation were still weighing on households.

evidence.claim: The mission said the authorities should reform fuel subsidies, contain current spending, and create space for targeted social transfers, while improving public investment and fiscal governance.
evidence.title: IMF Staff Completes 2022 Article IV and Program Review Mission to the Democratic Republic of the Congo
evidence.excerpt: The mission said the authorities should reform fuel subsidies, contain current spending, and create space for targeted social transfers, while improving public investment and fiscal governance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF mission statement with specific fiscal and distributional policy advice.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this concerns government policy choices under Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: The same statement notes significant downside risks and inflation pressures.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said poverty reduction had been elusive and the benefits from growth were not yet being shared more widely.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of Congo Economic Update: Harnessing Growth Through Digital Connectivity to Create Jobs and Reduce Poverty
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said poverty reduction had been elusive and the benefits from growth were not yet being shared more widely.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank country update with explicit welfare interpretation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: strong context and outcome evidence, but not all distributional outcomes are uniquely ruler-attributable.
contrary_evidence: The same update says economic resilience was strong and growth had rebounded.

evidence.claim: The Ministry of Budget's 2022 budget page shows the law on finances for 2022, Law No. 21/029 of 31 December 2021, and the linked budget documents for 2022.
evidence.title: Budget 2022
evidence.excerpt: The Ministry of Budget's 2022 budget page shows the law on finances for 2022, Law No. 21/029 of 31 December 2021, and the linked budget documents for 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official budget portal with the named 2022 finance law.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this is the incumbent government's approved fiscal framework.
contrary_evidence: Budget approval alone does not establish implementation quality.

evidence.claim: The 2022 budget proposal said the government would intensify the fight against corruption and revenue leakage, relying on expected improvements in commodity prices and better monetary and budget coordination.
evidence.title: Projet de Loi de Finances pour l'exercice 2022
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 budget proposal said the government would intensify the fight against corruption and revenue leakage, relying on expected improvements in commodity prices and better monetary and budget coordination.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official budget text with explicit anti-corruption and revenue claims.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: explicit government intent under the incumbent administration.
contrary_evidence: The budget text states the plan, not the realized outcome.

evidence.claim: The budget framework said revenue policy would raise domestic resources through anti-fraud and tax reforms, and it prioritized social and productive investment, east-region peace, and the 2023 general elections.
evidence.title: Projet de Loi de Finances pour l'exercice 2022
evidence.excerpt: The budget framework said revenue policy would raise domestic resources through anti-fraud and tax reforms, and it prioritized social and productive investment, east-region peace, and the 2023 general elections.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official budget framework with explicit policy priorities.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this is declared executive budget policy.
contrary_evidence: Announced priorities do not show execution quality.

evidence.claim: The project would support a single treasury account, better budget control, improved annual reporting, stronger oversight by the Court of Accounts, and enhanced civil-society participation in budgeting.
evidence.title: World Bank Supports the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Efforts to Improve Public Resources Management and Service Delivery
evidence.excerpt: The project would support a single treasury account, better budget control, improved annual reporting, stronger oversight by the Court of Accounts, and enhanced civil-society participation in budgeting.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary project design statement with concrete institutional reforms.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the reforms are tied to the incumbent government's public financial management agenda.
contrary_evidence: The statement itself implies the reforms were still needed, so this is not evidence of success by itself.

evidence.claim: The EITI Board commended the DRC for the timeliness of its disclosures and its thematic reports on SOEs, licensing, contract disclosure, beneficial ownership, subnational transfers, mining royalties, and barter-type infrastructure provisions.
evidence.title: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has achieved a high overall score in implementing the 2019 EITI Standard
evidence.excerpt: The EITI Board commended the DRC for the timeliness of its disclosures and its thematic reports on SOEs, licensing, contract disclosure, beneficial ownership, subnational transfers, mining royalties, and barter-type infrastructure provisions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent international validation of disclosure practices.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: strong institutional transparency evidence, but not a direct measure of household welfare.
contrary_evidence: The same decision says beneficial ownership and some newer standards were not yet fully implemented.

evidence.claim: The EITI Secretariat said the DRC had only partly met the beneficial-ownership objective and that only 21 of 77 significant extractive licensees submitted beneficial-ownership information in the cited report period.
evidence.title: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has achieved a high overall score in implementing the 2019 EITI Standard
evidence.excerpt: The EITI Secretariat said the DRC had only partly met the beneficial-ownership objective and that only 21 of 77 significant extractive licensees submitted beneficial-ownership information in the cited report period.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent validation report with a concrete quantitative gap.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this is about extractive-sector transparency under the incumbent government.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes some progress in open-format disclosure.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the Financial Action Task Force planned to place the DRC on its grey list for shortcomings in stamping out financial corruption, including money laundering and anti-terrorist financing.
evidence.title: Financial crime watchdog adds Congo to money laundering watch list
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that the Financial Action Task Force planned to place the DRC on its grey list for shortcomings in stamping out financial corruption, including money laundering and anti-terrorist financing.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-sourced report with clear attribution to FATF and finance ministry statements.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this is about national anti-corruption and financial controls under the incumbent administration.
contrary_evidence: The report also says officials would pursue the FATF recommendations and high-level commitment.

evidence.claim: OCCRP said the adviser described his closeness to President Felix Tshisekedi and was recorded offering access to mining licenses in exchange for a stake in a joint venture.
evidence.title: I Will Take My Percentage: Congolese Presidential Adviser Caught on Tape Negotiating Corrupt Mineral Deal
evidence.excerpt: OCCRP said the adviser described his closeness to President Felix Tshisekedi and was recorded offering access to mining licenses in exchange for a stake in a joint venture.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary investigative reporting with direct recording-based allegations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the conduct was tied to a close presidential adviser invoking access to Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: The recording appears to be an apparent sting operation, so the evidentiary chain should be kept explicit.

evidence.claim: HRW said Tshisekedi's administration had made many promises of reform but little action, and that corrupt and abusive practices and repression against journalists, activists, critics, and peaceful protesters had continued or escalated.
evidence.title: Child Labor and Human Rights Violations in the Mining Industry of the Democratic Republic of Congo
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Tshisekedi's administration had made many promises of reform but little action, and that corrupt and abusive practices and repression against journalists, activists, critics, and peaceful protesters had continued or escalated.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct testimony from a major rights NGO grounded in contemporaneous reporting.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 target-period governance and welfare evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: the statement explicitly assesses Tshisekedi's administration.
contrary_evidence: The same testimony notes some positive early steps such as releasing political prisoners.

evidence.claim: The DRC's free-primary-schooling reform had expanded access by June 2022, with the World Bank saying enrollment had risen by about 3 million children and the nationwide grievance hotline 'Allo Ecole' was functional.
evidence.title: Free Primary Schooling in the DRC: Progress Despite the Perils
evidence.excerpt: The DRC's free-primary-schooling reform had expanded access by June 2022, with the World Bank saying enrollment had risen by about 3 million children and the nationwide grievance hotline 'Allo Ecole' was functional.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary institutional blog by World Bank staff, directly dated and describing implementation details and outputs in 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 execution of a major government social-spending reform that began in 2019 but was still being implemented in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong but not exclusive: the reform is a Tshisekedi-administration policy, with World Bank co-financing and implementation support.
contrary_evidence: The same source notes teacher strikes, salary-payment problems, and fraud findings in the education sector.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said the government had liberalized the telecommunications sector by publishing a new Telecommunications Law, but secondary legislation, fiber-backbone development, PPPs, and tax simplification were still needed to operationalize the reform.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of Congo Economic Update: Harnessing Growth Through Digital Connectivity to Create Jobs and Reduce Poverty
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said the government had liberalized the telecommunications sector by publishing a new Telecommunications Law, but secondary legislation, fiber-backbone development, PPPs, and tax simplification were still needed to operationalize the reform.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct institutional assessment of a 2022 policy change and its next implementation steps.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in-period for 2022 policy design and implementation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: this reflects an administration-backed regulatory reform, though execution depends on ministers and regulators beyond the president alone.
contrary_evidence: The same source says major challenges remained and that the law still required secondary legislation to become fully operational.

evidence.claim: The DRC's beneficial-ownership disclosure regime was still only partly met in 2022: there was no public beneficial-ownership registry and the legal framework for reporting was still incomplete.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo | EITI
evidence.excerpt: The DRC's beneficial-ownership disclosure regime was still only partly met in 2022: there was no public beneficial-ownership registry and the legal framework for reporting was still incomplete.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: EITI validation summary is an authoritative, dated assessment of implementation quality and gaps.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the target year and the extractive-governance environment relevant to 2022 economic stewardship.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the gap reflects government-level failure to fully operationalize transparency rules under the Tshisekedi administration.
contrary_evidence: The same EITI page also records systematic disclosure improvements and a higher transparency score in other extractive-data areas.

evidence.claim: By December 2022, the STEP social-protection program had improved access to livelihoods for 530,000 beneficiaries, including more than 200,000 women, and upgraded 2,185 community infrastructures such as schools and clinics.
evidence.title: Providing safety nets for the most vulnerable in the Democratic Republic of Congo: Incremental steps with a large footprint
evidence.excerpt: By December 2022, the STEP social-protection program had improved access to livelihoods for 530,000 beneficiaries, including more than 200,000 women, and upgraded 2,185 community infrastructures such as schools and clinics.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Result note from the World Bank with a clear end-2022 outcome statement and specific beneficiary counts.
evidence.period_fit: Published in 2023 but explicitly reports outcomes through December 2022, so the temporal fit is good for the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is a donor-backed safety-net program, but it reflects the broader administration's social-protection environment and implementation capacity.
contrary_evidence: The result page is retrospective and donor-mediated, so it does not isolate direct presidential causation.

evidence.claim: UNICEF reported that more than 4,000 vulnerable families in N'Sele received unconditional cash transfers that helped them pay school costs and improve access to basic social services.
evidence.title: Children’s education, a priority for Marlène
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF reported that more than 4,000 vulnerable families in N'Sele received unconditional cash transfers that helped them pay school costs and improve access to basic social services.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF provides a concrete beneficiary example from a documented cash-transfer program, though the page is a human-interest story rather than an audit.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to household-level welfare support in the ruler-period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the intervention is donor-backed and local, but it evidences delivery of a broader social-protection and education-support environment under Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: This is a localized intervention and does not prove national-scale distributional success.

evidence.claim: The central bank's 2022 annual report said its priorities were to strengthen confidence in the Congolese franc, reduce dependence on foreign currency in domestic transactions, digitize payments, automate controls, and use monetary policy as a lever for inclusive development and social protection.
evidence.title: Rapport Annuel 2022
evidence.excerpt: The central bank's 2022 annual report said its priorities were to strengthen confidence in the Congolese franc, reduce dependence on foreign currency in domestic transactions, digitize payments, automate controls, and use monetary policy as a lever for inclusive development and social protection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official annual-report foreword from the central bank governor, dated to the target year, with explicit policy orientation but not audited outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: the BCC is institutionally separate, so this is better read as administration-level macro governance than direct presidential control.
contrary_evidence: The passage states priorities, not realized outcomes, and does not by itself show successful stabilization.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 nuclear/existential-risk decision by Tshisekedi is evidenced, and the package never shows operational nuclear control, brinkmanship, or safeguard intervention.
Direct 2022 execution and household/distribution outcome evidence remains thinner than the policy and macro coverage.
Direct, nationally representative 2022 welfare-outcome evidence attributable to Tshisekedi remains limited relative to the amount of partner-led program evidence.

Direct personal-nexus evidence is still sparse: no clear 2022 asset-declaration, campaign-finance, beneficial-ownership, or court/audit record ties Tshisekedi himself to self-dealing or deliberate deception.
Independent, audited delivery and outcome evidence is thinner than the program rhetoric and internal reporting.
